titulo: Reduced Relatives, Participle Clauses and Nominalisation
subtitulo: Dense writing about the housing market
descripcion: The density that separates C1 writing from B2 writing comes from three devices working together: dropping the relative pronoun, compressing a clause into a participle, and turning a verb into a noun. Used separately, each one saves a few words. Used together in the same paragraph, they produce the compact, confident register of a strong report.

cuadroReferencia.notaPie: Combining all three in one sentence is normal in a report; combining them in speech reads as stiff. Match the density to the register.

ejemplos.texto: Having been delayed twice, the report published last week drew immediate criticism.
The team's quick decision, taken under pressure, avoided a bigger loss.
Data collected over three years, though incomplete, still points the same way.

notas: A reduced relative only works when the missing pronoun would have been the subject; the report I read cannot become the report read by me here.
Nominalising every verb in a paragraph makes it unreadable; alternate nominal and verbal sentences.
A dangling participle is the most common failure of this combination: the participle's implied subject must match the main clause's subject.

es.en: Spanish tolerates an implicit, ambiguous subject in gerund constructions much better (estando en Madrid, me llamaron), while English requires the subject of the participle to match that of the main clause. Spanish speakers produce dangling participles precisely because the construction is acceptable in Spanish.
es.es: El español tolera mucho mejor un sujeto implícito y ambiguo en construcciones de gerundio («estando en Madrid, me llamaron»), mientras que el inglés exige que el sujeto del participio coincida con el del verbo principal. Precisamente por eso los hispanohablantes producen dangling participles: la construcción equivalente sí es aceptable en español.

de.en: German nominalises readily, so the nominalisation part of this cluster is easy for German speakers. The difference lies in the reduced relative, which English places after the noun where German uses a prenominal participle phrase, and in keeping participle clauses tied to the subject of the main clause.
de.de: Deutsch nominalisiert sehr leicht, daher ist dieser Teil für Deutschsprachige unkompliziert. Der Unterschied liegt im reduced relative, das im Englischen nach dem Substantiv steht, während Deutsch eine vorangestellte Partizipgruppe verwendet, und darin, Partizipialsätze eindeutig auf das Subjekt des Hauptsatzes zu beziehen.

it.en: Postnominal participles are native to Italian, and bureaucratic Italian nominalises heavily, so two of the three devices come easily. The risk is the dangling participle or gerund, which colloquial Italian tolerates much more than written English.
it.it: I participi postnominali sono naturali in italiano e l'italiano burocratico nominalizza molto, quindi due dei tre dispositivi risultano facili. Il rischio è il dangling participle o gerund, che l'italiano colloquiale tollera molto più dell'inglese scritto.

fr.en: Formal French nominalises readily and uses postnominal participles, and French speakers know the same-subject rule for the gérondif. This cluster is therefore relatively easy for them; the main risk is over-compressing texts in genres where English prefers a verbal style.
fr.fr: Le français formel nominalise facilement et utilise des participes postposés, et les francophones connaissent la règle du même sujet pour le gérondif. Ce groupe de structures est donc relativement facile ; le principal risque est de trop compresser dans des genres où l'anglais préfère un style verbal.

pt.en: Postnominal participles are native to Portuguese, but the personal infinitive lets Portuguese stay verbal where English nominalises. Portuguese speakers therefore tend to under-nominalise and, especially in Brazilian usage, to produce dangling gerund clauses.
pt.pt: Particípios depois do substantivo são naturais em português, mas o infinitivo pessoal permite manter a redação verbal onde o inglês nominaliza. Falantes de português tendem, portanto, a nominalizar pouco e, especialmente no uso brasileiro, a produzir orações de gerúndio com sujeito solto.

errores: Producing a dangling participle where the implied subject doesn't match the main clause.
Reducing a relative clause where the missing pronoun would be the object, which isn't grammatically allowed.
Nominalising every sentence in a row until the paragraph becomes unreadable.

es: *realización* rendered as *realisation*: *the realisation of the study* instead of *carrying out the study*.
de: Building *of*-chains from German genitive chains: *the checking of the calculation of the loads* instead of *checking the load calculation*.
it: *effettuare* rendered as *effectuate*: *to effectuate a check* instead of *to carry out a check*.
fr: *réalisation* rendered as *realisation*: *the realisation of the project* instead of *completing the project*.
pt: *realização* rendered as *realisation*: *the realisation of the study* instead of *carrying out the study*.

mision.consigna: Write a paragraph for a report on the housing situation in a city you know.
requisitos: two nominalisations replacing a full clause (*the landlord's decision to…*)
use *the housing market*, *a tenancy agreement* and *utility costs*

microtareas.texto: Take three full sentences about renting and compress them into one.
Turn five verbs about *a viewing* into nouns and use each in a phrase.
Rewrite a paragraph you wrote at B2 level about being *priced out* with all three devices.

autochequeo: Is the reduced pronoun always the subject, never the object, of its clause?
Does every participle's implied subject match the main clause's subject?
Is the paragraph a mix of nominal and verbal sentences, not all one or the other?
Would the density fit a spoken conversation, or does it belong only in writing?
Is at least one dangling participle risk checked and fixed?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on reduced relatives, participle clauses and nominalisation. Flag every dangling participle, check whether reductions are grammatically allowed, and say whether the density fits the register. Do not rewrite the text.
